title: H5019 · N@buwkadne'tstsar
text:
or Nbukadneotstsar (2 Kings 24:1, 10) {neb-oo-kad-nets-tsar'}; or Nbuwkadnetstsar (Esther 2:6; Daniel 1:18) {neb-oo-kad-nets-tsar'}; or Nbuwkadreotstsar {neb-oo-kad-rets-tsar'}; or Nbuwkadreltstsowr (Ezra 2:1; Jeremiah 49:28) {neb-oo-kad-rets-tsore'}; or foreign derivation; Nebukadnetstsar (or -retstsar, or -retstsor), king of Babylon:--Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadrezzar. 
 

See  H10

title: H5020 · N@buwkadnetstsar (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 5019:--Nebuchadnezzar. 
 

See  H5019

title: H5021 · N@buwshazban
text: of foreign derivation; Nebushazban, Nebuchadnezzar's chief eunuch:--Nebushazban.

title: H5022 · Nabowth
text:
feminine plural from the same as 5011; fruits; Naboth, an Israelite:--Naboth. 
 

See  H5011

title: H5023 · n@bizbah (Aramaic)
text: (Aramaic) of uncertain derivation; a largess:--reward.

title: H5024 · nabach
text: a primitive root; to bark (as a dog):--bark.

title: H5025 · Nobach
text:
from 5024; a bark; Nobach, the name of an Israelite, and of a place East of the Jordan:--Nobah. 
 

See  H5024

title: H5026 · Nibchaz
text: of foreign origin; Nibchaz, a deity of the Avites:--Nibhaz.

title: H5027 · nabat
text: a primitive root; to scan, i.e. look intently at; by implication, to regard with pleasure, favor or care:--(cause to) behold, consider, look (down), regard, have respect, see.

title: H5028 · N@bat
text:
from 5027; regard; Nebat, the father of Jeroboam I:--Nebat. 
 

See  H5027

title: H5029 · n@biy' (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 5030; a prophet:--prophet. 
 

See  H5030

title: H5030 · nabiy'
text:
from 5012; a prophet or (generally) inspired man:--prophecy, that prophesy, prophet. 
 

See  H5012

title: H5031 · n@biy'ah
text:
feminine of 5030; a prophetess or (generally) inspired woman; by implication, a poetess; by association a prophet's wife:--prophetess. 
 

See  H5030

title: H5032 · N@bayowth
text:
or Nbayoth {neb-aw-yoth'}; feminine plural from 5107; fruitfulnesses; Nebajoth, a son of Ismael, and the country settled by him:--Nebaioth, Nebajoth. 
 

See  H5107

title: H5033 · nebek
text: from an unused root meaning to burst forth; a fountain:--spring.

title: H5034 · nabel
text: a primitive root; to wilt; generally, to fall away, fail, faint; figuratively, to be foolish or (morally) wicked; causatively, to despise, disgrace:--disgrace, dishounour, lightly esteem, fade (away, - ing), fall (down, -ling, off), do foolishly, come to nought, X surely, make vile, wither.

title: H5035 · nebel
text:
or nebel {nay'-bel}; from 5034; a skin-bag for liquids (from collapsing when empty); hence, a vase (as similar in shape when full); also a lyre (as having a body of like form):--bottle, pitcher, psaltery, vessel, viol. 
 

See  H5034

title: H5036 · nabal
text:
from 5034; stupid; wicked (especially impious):-- fool(-ish, -ish man, -ish woman), vile person. 
 

See  H5034

title: H5037 · Nabal
text:
the same as 5036; dolt; Nabal, an Israelite:--Nabal. 
 

See  H5036

title: H5038 · n@belah
text:
from 5034; a flabby thing, i.e. a carcase or carrion (human or bestial, often collectively); figuratively, an idol:-- (dead) body, (dead) carcase, dead of itself, which died, (beast) that (which) dieth of itself. 
 

See  H5034

title: H5039 · n@balah
text:
feminine of 5036; foolishness, i.e. (morally) wickedness; concretely, a crime; by extension, punishment:--folly, vile, villany. 
 

See  H5036

title: H5040 · nabluwth
text:
from 5036; properly, disgrace, i.e. the (female) pudenda:--lewdness. 
 

See  H5036

title: H5041 · N@ballat
text:
apparently from 5036 and 3909; foolish secrecy; Neballat, a place in Palestine:--Neballat. 
 

See  H5036  
See  H3909

title: H5042 · naba`
text: a primitive root; to gush forth; figuratively, to utter (good or bad words); specifically, to emit (a foul odor):--belch out, flowing, pour out, send forth, utter (abundantly).

title: H5043 · nebr@sha' (Aramaic)
text: (Aramaic) from an unused root meaning to shine; a light; plural (collectively) a chandelier:--candlestick.

title: H5044 · Nibshan
text: of uncertain derivation; Nibshan, a place in Palestine:--Nibshan.

title: H5045 · negeb
text: from an unused root meaning to be parched; the south (from its drought); specifically, the Negeb or southern district of Judah, occasionally, Egypt (as south to Palestine):--south (country, side, -ward).

title: H5046 · nagad
text: a primitive root; properly, to front, i.e. stand boldly out opposite; by implication (causatively), to manifest; figuratively, to announce (always by word of mouth to one present); specifically, to expose, predict, explain, praise:--bewray, X certainly, certify, declare(-ing), denounce, expound, X fully, messenger, plainly, profess, rehearse, report, shew (forth), speak, X surely, tell, utter.

title: H5047 · n@gad (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 5046; to flow (through the idea of clearing the way):--issue. 
 

See  H5046

title: H5048 · neged
text:
from 5046; a front, i.e. part opposite; specifically a counterpart, or mate; usually (adverbial, especially with preposition) over against or before:--about, (over) against, X aloof, X far (off), X from, over, presence, X other side, sight, X to view. 
 

See  H5046

title: H5049 · neged (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 5048; opposite:--toward. 
 

See  H5048

title: H5050 · nagahh
text: a primitive root; to glitter; causatively, to illuminate:--(en-)lighten, (cause to) shine.

title: H5051 · nogahh
text:
from 5050; brilliancy (literally or figuratively):--bright(-ness), light, (clear) shining. 
 

See  H5050

title: H5052 · Nogahh
text:
the same as 5051; Nogah, a son of David:--Nogah. 
 

See  H5051

title: H5053 · nogahh (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 5051; dawn:--morning. 
 

See  H5051

title: H5054 · n@gohah
text:
feminine of 5051; splendor:--brightness. 
 

See  H5051

title: H5055 · nagach
text: a primitive root; to but with the horns; figuratively, to war against:--gore, push (down, -ing).

title: H5056 · naggach
text:
from 5055; butting, i.e. vicious:--used (wont) to push. 
 

See  H5055

title: H5057 · nagiyd
text:
or nagid {naw-gheed'}; from 5046; a commander (as occupying the front), civil, military or religious; generally (abstractly, plural), honorable themes:--captain, chief, excellent thing, (chief) governor, leader, noble, prince, (chief) ruler. 
 

See  H5046

title: H5058 · n@giynah
text:
or ngiynath (Psa. 61:title) {neg-ee-nath'}; from 5059; properly, instrumental music; by implication, a stringed instrument; by extension, a poem set to music; specifically, an epigram:--stringed instrument, musick, Neginoth (plural), song. 
 

See  H5059

title: H5059 · nagan
text: a primitive root; properly, to thrum, i.e. beat a tune with the fingers; expec. to play on a stringed instrument; hence (generally), to make music:--player on instruments, sing to the stringed instruments, melody, ministrel, play(-er, -ing).

title: H5060 · naga`
text: a primitive root; properly, to touch, i.e. lay the hand upon (for any purpose; euphem., to lie with a woman); by implication, to reach (figuratively, to arrive, acquire); violently, to strike (punish, defeat, destroy, etc.):--beat, (X be able to) bring (down), cast, come (nigh), draw near (nigh), get up, happen, join, near, plague, reach (up), smite, strike, touch.

title: H5061 · nega`
text:
from 5060; a blow (figuratively, infliction); also (by implication) a spot (concretely, a leprous person or dress):--plague, sore, stricken, stripe, stroke, wound. 
 

See  H5060

title: H5062 · nagaph
text: a primitive root; to push, gore, defeat, stub (the toe), inflict (a disease):--beat, dash, hurt, plague, slay, smite (down), strike, stumble, X surely, put to the worse.

title: H5063 · negeph
text:
from 5062; a trip (of the foot); figuratively, an infliction (of disease):--plague, stumbling. 
 

See  H5062

title: H5064 · nagar
text: a primitive root; to flow; figuratively, to stretch out; causatively, to pour out or down; figuratively, to deliver over:--fall, flow away, pour down (out), run, shed, spilt, trickle down.

title: H5065 · nagas
text: a primitive root; to drive (an animal, a workman, a debtor, an army); by implication, to tax, harass, tyrannize:--distress, driver, exact(-or), oppress(-or), X  raiser of taxes, taskmaster.

title: H5066 · nagash
text: a primitive root; to be or come (causatively, bring) near (for any purpose); euphemistically, to lie with a woman; as an enemy, to attack; relig. to worship; causatively, to present; figuratively, to adduce an argument; by reversal, to stand back:--(make to) approach (nigh), bring (forth, hither, near), (cause to) come (hither, near, nigh), give place, go hard (up), (be, draw, go) near (nigh), offer, overtake, present, put, stand.

title: H5067 · ned
text:
from 5110 in the sense of piling up; a mound, i.e. wave:--heap. 
 

See  H5110

title: H5068 · nadab
text: a primitive root; to impel; hence, to volunteer (as a soldier), to present spontaneously:--offer freely, be (give, make, offer self) willing(-ly).

title: H5069 · n@dab (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 5068; be (or give) liberal(-ly):--(be minded of...own) freewill (offering), offer freely (willingly). 
 

See  H5068

title: H5070 · Nadab
text:
from 5068; liberal; Nadab, the name of four Israelites:--Nadab. 
 

See  H5068

title: H5071 · n@dabah
text:
from 5068; properly (abstractly) spontaneity, or (adjectively) spontaneous; also (concretely) a spontaneous or (by inference, in plural) abundant gift:--free(-will) offering, freely, plentiful, voluntary(-ily, offering), willing(-ly), offering). 
 

See  H5068

title: H5072 · N@dabyah
text:
from 5068 and 3050; largess of Jah; Nedabjah, an Israelite:--Nedabiah. 
 

See  H5068  
See  H3050

title: H5073 · nidbak (Aramaic)
text: (Aramaic) from a root meaning to stick; a layer (of building materials):--row.

title: H5074 · nadad
text: a primitive root; properly, to wave to and fro (rarely to flap up and down); figuratively, to rove, flee, or (causatively) to drive away:--chase (away), X could not, depart, flee (X apace, away), (re-)move, thrust away, wander (abroad, -er, -ing).

title: H5075 · n@dad (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 5074; to depart:--go from. 
 

See  H5074

title: H5076 · nadud
text:
passive participle of 5074; properly, tossed; abstractly, a rolling (on the bed):--tossing to and fro. 
 

See  H5074

title: H5077 · nadah
text: or nada  (2 Kings 17:21) {naw-daw'}; a primitive root; properly, to toss; figuratively, to exclude, i.e. banish, postpone, prohibit:--cast out, drive, put far away.

title: H5078 · nedeh
text:
from 5077 in the sense of freely flinging money; a bounty (for prostitution):--gifts. 
 

See  H5077

title: H5079 · niddah
text:
from 5074; properly, rejection; by implication, impurity, especially personal (menstruation) or moral (idolatry, incest):--X far, filthiness, X flowers, menstruous (woman), put apart, X removed (woman), separation, set apart, unclean(-ness, thing, with filthiness). 
 

See  H5074

title: H5080 · nadach
text: a primitive root; to push off; used in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively (to expel, mislead, strike, inflict, etc.):--banish, bring, cast down (out), chase, compel, draw away, drive (away, out, quite), fetch a stroke, force, go away, outcast, thrust away (out), withdraw.

title: H5081 · nadiyb
text:
from 5068; properly, voluntary, i.e. generous; hence, magnanimous; as noun, a grandee (sometimes a tyrant):--free, liberal (things), noble, prince, willing ((hearted)). 
 

See  H5068

title: H5082 · n@diybah
text:
feminine of 5081; properly, nobility, i.e. reputation:--soul. 
 

See  H5081

title: H5083 · nadan
text: probably from an unused root meaning to give; a present (for prostitution):--gift.

title: H5084 · nadan
text: of uncertain derivation; a sheath (of a sword):--sheath.

title: H5085 · nidneh (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) from the same as 5084; a sheath; figuratively, the body (as the receptacle of the soul):--body. 
 

See  H5084

title: H5086 · nadaph
text: a primitive root; to shove asunder, i.e. disperse:--drive (away, to and fro), thrust down, shaken, tossed to and fro.

title: H5087 · nadar
text: a primitive root; to promise (pos., to do or give something to God):--(make a) vow.

title: H5088 · neder
text:
or neder {nay'-der}; from 5087; a promise (to God); also (concretely) a thing promised:--vow((-ed)). 
 

See  H5087

title: H5089 · noahh
text: from an unused root meaning to lament; lamentation:--wailing.

title: H5090 · nahag
text: a primitive root; to drive forth (a person, an animal or chariot), i.e. lead, carry away; reflexively, to proceed (i.e. impel or guide oneself); also (from the panting induced by effort), to sigh:--acquaint, bring (away), carry away, drive (away), lead (away, forth), (be) guide, lead (away, forth).

title: H5091 · nahah
text: a primitive root; to groan, i.e. bewail; hence (through the idea of crying aloud), to assemble (as if on proclamation):-- lament, wail.

title: H5092 · n@hiy
text:
from 5091; an elegy:--lamentation, wailing. 
 

See  H5091

title: H5093 · nihyah
text:
feminine of 5092; lamentation:--doleful. 
 

See  H5092

title: H5094 · n@hiyr (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) or nehiyruw (Aramaic) {neh-hee-roo'}; from the same as 5105; illumination, i.e. (figuratively) wisdom:--light. 
 

See  H5105

title: H5095 · nahal
text: a primitive root; properly, to run with a sparkle, i.e. flow; hence (transitively), to conduct, and (by inference) to protect, sustain:--carry, feed, guide, lead (gently, on).

title: H5096 · Nahalal
text:
or Nahalol {nah-hal-ole'}; the same as 5097; Nahalal or Nahalol, a place in Palestine:--Nahalal, Nahallal, Nahalol. 
 

See  H5097

title: H5097 · nahalol
text:
from 5095; pasture:--bush. 
 

See  H5095

title: H5098 · naham
text: a primitive root; to growl:--mourn, roar(-ing).

title: H5099 · naham
text:
from 5098; a snarl:--roaring. 
 

See  H5098

title: H5100 · n@hamah
text:
feminine of 5099; snarling:--disquietness, roaring. 
 

See  H5099

title: H5101 · nahaq
text: a primitive root; to bray (as an ass), scream (from hunger:--bray.

title: H5102 · nahar
text: a primitive root; to sparkle, i.e. (figuratively) be cheerful; hence (from the sheen of a running stream) to flow, i.e. (figuratively) assemble:--flow (together), be lightened.

title: H5103 · n@har (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) from a root corresponding to 5102; a river, especially the Euphrates:--river, stream. 
 

See  H5102

title: H5104 · nahar
text:
from 5102; a stream (including the sea; expec. the Nile, Euphrates, etc.); figuratively, prosperity:--flood, river. 
 

See  H5102

title: H5105 · n@harah
text:
from 5102 in its original sense; daylight:--light. 
 

See  H5102

title: H5106 · nuw'
text: a primitive root; to refuse, forbid, dissuade, or neutralize:--break, disallow, discourage, make of none effect.

title: H5107 · nuwb
text: a primitive root; to germinate, i.e. (figuratively) to (causatively, make) flourish; also (of words), to utter:--bring forth (fruit), make cheerful, increase.

title: H5108 · nowb
text:
or neyb {nabe}; from 5107; produce, literally or figuratively:--fruit. 
 

See  H5107

title: H5109 · Nowbay
text:
from 5108; fruitful; Nobai, an Israelite:--Nebai (from the margin). 
 

See  H5108

title: H5110 · nuwd
text: a primitive root; to nod, i.e. waver; figuratively, to wander, flee, disappear; also (from shaking the head in sympathy), to console, deplore, or (from tossing the head in scorn) taunt:--bemoan, flee, get, mourn, make to move, take pity, remove, shake, skip for joy, be sorry, vagabond, way, wandering.

title: H5111 · nuwd (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 5116; to flee:--get away. 
 

See  H5116

title: H5112 · nowd
text:
(only defect. nod {node}); from 5110; exile:--wandering. 
 

See  H5110

title: H5113 · Nowd
text:
the same as 5112; vagrancy; Nod, the land of Cain:--Nod. 
 

See  H5112

title: H5114 · Nowdab
text:
from 5068; noble; Nodab, an Arab tribe:--Nodab. 
 

See  H5068

title: H5115 · navah
text:
a primitive root; to rest (as at home); causatively (through the implied idea of beauty (compare 5116)), to celebrate (with praises):--keept at home, prepare an habitation. 
 

See  H5116

title: H5116 · naveh
text:
or (feminine) navah {naw-vaw'}; from 5115; (adjectively) at home; hence (by implication of satisfaction) lovely; also (noun) a home, of God (temple), men (residence), flocks (pasture), or wild animals (den):--comely, dwelling (place), fold, habitation, pleasant place, sheepcote, stable, tarried. 
 

See  H5115

title: H5117 · nuwach
text:
a primitive root; to rest, i.e. settle down; used in a great variety of applications, literal and figurative, intransitive, transitive and causative (to dwell, stay, let fall, place, let alone, withdraw, give comfort, etc.):--cease, be confederate, lay, let down, (be) quiet, remain, (cause to, be at, give, have, make to) rest, set down. Compare 3241. 
 

See  H3241

title: H5118 · nuwach
text:
or nowach {no'-akh}; from 5117; quiet:--rest(-ed, -ing place). 
 

See  H5117

title: H5119 · Nowchah
text:
feminine of 5118; quietude; Nochah, an Israelite:--Nohah. 
 

See  H5118

title: H5120 · nuwt
text: to quake:--be moved.

title: H5121 · Naviyth
text:
from 5115; residence; Navith, a place in Palestine:--Naioth (from the margin). 
 

See  H5115

title: H5122 · n@valuw (Aramaic)
text: (Aramaic) or nvaliy (Aramaic) {nev-aw-lee'}; from an unused root probably meaning to be foul; a sink:--dunghill.

title: H5123 · nuwm
text: a primitive root; to slumber (from drowsiness):--sleep, slumber.

title: H5124 · nuwmah
text:
from 5123; sleepiness:--drowsiness. 
 

See  H5123

title: H5125 · nuwn
text: a primitive root; to resprout, i.e. propagate by shoots; figuratively, to be perpetual:--be continued.

title: H5126 · Nuwn
text:
or Nown (1 Chron. 7:27) {nohn}; from 5125; perpetuity, Nun or Non, the father of Joshua:--Non, Nun. 
 

See  H5125

title: H5127 · nuwc
text: a primitive root; to flit, i.e. vanish away (subside, escape; causatively, chase, impel, deliver):--X abate, away, be displayed, (make to) flee (away, -ing), put to flight, X hide, lift up a standard.

title: H5128 · nuwa`
text: a primitive root; to waver, in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively (as subjoined):--continually, fugitive, X make, to (go) up and down, be gone away, (be) move(-able, -d), be promoted, reel, remove, scatter, set, shake, sift, stagger, to and fro, be vagabond, wag, (make) wander (up and down).

title: H5129 · Now`adyah
text:
from 3259 and 3050; convened of Jah; Noadjah, the name of an Israelite, and a false prophetess:--Noadiah. 
 

See  H3259  
See  H3050

title: H5130 · nuwph
text: a primitive root; to quiver (i.e. vibrate up and down, or rock to and fro); used in a great variety of applications (including sprinkling, beckoning, rubbing, bastinadoing, sawing, waving, etc.):--lift up, move, offer, perfume, send, shake, sift, strike, wave.

title: H5131 · nowph
text:
from 5130; elevation:--situation. Compare 5297. 
 

See  H5130  
See  H5297

title: H5132 · nuwts
text: a primitive root; properly, to flash; hence, to blossom (from the brilliancy of color); also, to fly away (from the quickness of motion):--flee away, bud (forth).

title: H5133 · nowtsah
text:
or notsah {no-tsaw'}; feminine active participle of 5327 in the sense of flying; a pinion (or wing feather); often (collectively) plumage:--feather(-s), ostrich. 
 

See  H5327

title: H5134 · nuwq
text: a primitive root; to suckle:--nurse.

title: H5135 · nuwr (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) from an unused root (corresponding to that of 5216) meaning to shine; fire:--fiery, fire. 
 

See  H5216

title: H5136 · nuwsh
text: a primitive root; to be sick, i.e. (figuratively) distressed:--be full of heaviness.

title: H5137 · nazah
text: a primitive root; to spirt, i.e. besprinkle (especially in expiation):--sprinkle.

title: H5138 · naziyd
text:
from 2102; something boiled, i.e. soup:--pottage. 
 

See  H2102

title: H5139 · naziyr
text:
or nazir {naw-zeer'}; from 5144; separate, i.e. consecrated (as prince, a Nazirite); hence (figuratively from the latter) an unpruned vine (like an unshorn Nazirite):--Nazarite (by a false alliteration with Nazareth), separate(-d), vine undressed. 
 

See  H5144

title: H5140 · nazal
text: a primitive root; to drip, or shed by trickling:--distil, drop, flood, (cause to) flow(-ing), gush out, melt, pour (down), running water, stream.

title: H5141 · nexem
text: from an unused root of uncertain meaning;  a nose-ring:--earring, jewel.

title: H5142 · n@zaq (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to the root of 5143; to suffer (causatively, inflict) loss:--have (en-)damage, hurt(-ful). 
 

See  H5143

title: H5143 · nezeq
text: from an unused root meaning to injure; loss:--damage.

title: H5144 · nazar
text: a primitive root; to hold aloof, i.e. (intransitivey) abstain (from food and drink, from impurity, and even from divine worship (i.e. apostatize)); specifically, to set apart (to sacred purposes), i.e. devote:--consecrate, separate(-ing, self).

title: H5145 · nezer
text:
or nezer {nay'-zer}; from 5144; properly, something set apart, i.e. (abstractly) dedication (of a priet or Nazirite); hence (concretely) unshorn locks; also (by implication) a chaplet (especially of royalty):--consecration, crown, hair, separation. 
 

See  H5144

title: H5146 · Noach
text:
the same as 5118; rest; Noach, the patriarch of the flood:--Noah. 
 

See  H5118

title: H5147 · Nachbiy
text:
from 2247; occult; Nachbi, an Israelite:--Nakbi. 
 

See  H2247

title: H5148 · nachah
text: a primitive root; to guide; by implication, to transport (into exile, or as colonists):--bestow, bring, govern, guide, lead (forth), put, straiten.

title: H5149 · N@chuwm
text:
from 5162; comforted; Nechum, an Israelite:--Nehum. 
 

See  H5162

title: H5150 · nichuwm
text:
or nichum {nee-khoom'}; from 5162; properly, consoled; abstractly, solace:--comfort(-able), repenting. 
 

See  H5162

title: H5151 · Nachuwm
text:
from 5162; comfortable; Nachum, an Israelite prophet:--Nahum. 
 

See  H5162

title: H5152 · Nachowr
text:
from the same as 5170; snorer; Nochor, the name of the grandfather and a brother of Abraham:--Nahor. 
 

See  H5170

title: H5153 · nachuwsh
text:
apparently passive participle of 5172 (perhaps in the sense of ringing, i.e. bell-metal; or from the red color of the throat of a serpent (5175, as denominative) when hissing); coppery, i.e. (figuratively) hard:--of brass. 
 

See  H5172  
See  H5175

title: H5154 · n@chuwshah
text:
or nchushah {nekh-oo-shaw'}; feminine of 5153; copper:--brass, steel. Compare 5176. 
 

See  H5153

title: H7848 · shittah
text:
feminine of a derivative (only in the plural shittiym {shit-teem'}; meaning the sticks of wood) from the same as 7850; the acacia (from its scourging thorns):--shittah, shittim. See also 1029. 
 

See  H7850  
See  H1029

title: H7849 · shatach
text: a primitive root; to expand:--all abroad, enlarge, spread, stretch out.

title: H7850 · shotet
text:
active participle of an otherwise unused root meaning (properly, to pierce; but only as a denominative from 7752) to flog; a goad:--scourge. 
 

See  H7752

title: H7851 · Shittiym
text:
the same as the plural of 7848; acacia trees; Shittim, a place East of the Jordan:--Shittim. 
 

See  H7848

title: H7852 · satam
text: a primitive root; properly, to lurk for, i.e. persecute:--hate, oppose self against.

title: H7853 · satan
text: a primitive root; to attack, (figuratively) accuse:--(be an) adversary, resist.

title: H7854 · satan
text:
from 7853; an opponent; especially (with the article prefixed) Satan, the arch-enemy of good:--adversary, Satan, withstand. 
 

See  H7853

title: H7855 · sitnah
text:
from 7853; opposition (by letter):--accusation. 
 

See  H7853

title: H7856 · Sitnah
text:
the same as 7855; Sitnah, the name of a well in Pal:--Sitnah. 
 

See  H7855

title: H7857 · shataph
text: a primitive root; to gush; by implication, to inundate, cleanse; by analogy, to gallop, conquer:--drown, (over-)flow(- whelm, rinse, run, rush, (throughly) wash (away).

title: H7858 · sheteph
text:
or sheteph {shay'-tef}; from 7857; a deluge (literally or figuratively):--flood, outrageous, overflowing. 
 

See  H7857

title: H7859 · sh@tar (Aramaic)
text: (Aramaic) of uncertain derivation; a side:--side.

title: H7860 · shoter
text: active participle of an otherwise unused root probably meaning to write; properly, a scribe, i.e. (by analogy or implication) an official superintendent or magistrate:--officer, overseer, ruler.

title: H7861 · Shitray
text:
from the same as 7860; magisterial; Shitrai, an Israelite:--Shitrai. 
 

See  H7860

title: H7862 · shay
text:
probably from 7737; a gift (as available):--present. 
 

See  H7737

title: H7863 · siy'
text:
from the same as 7721 by permutation; elevation:-- excellency. 
 

See  H7721

title: H7864 · Sh@ya'
text:
for 7724; Sheja, an Israelite:--Sheva (from the margin). 
 

See  H7724

title: H7865 · Siy'on
text:
from 7863; peak; Sion, the summit of Mt. Hermon:--Sion. 
 

See  H7863

title: H7866 · Shi'yown
text:
from the same as 7722; ruin; Shijon, a place in Palestine --Shihon. 
 

See  H7722

title: H7867 · siyb
text: a primitive root; properly, to become aged, i.e. (by implication) to grow gray:--(be) grayheaded.

title: H7868 · siyb (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 7867:--elder. 
 

See  H7867

title: H7869 · seyb
text:
from 7867; old age:--age. 
 

See  H7867

title: H7870 · shiybah
text:
by permutation from 7725; a return (of property):--captivity. 
 

See  H7725

title: H7871 · shiybah
text:
from 3427; residence:--while...lay. 
 

See  H3427

title: H7872 · seybah
text:
feminine of 7869; old age:--(be) gray (grey hoar,-y) hairs (head,-ed), old age. 
 

See  H7869

title: H7873 · siyg
text:
from 7734; a withdrawal (into a private place):--pursuing. 
 

See  H7734

title: H7874 · siyd
text:
a primitive root probably meaning to boil up (compare 7736); used only as denominative from 7875; to plaster:--plaister. 
 

See  H7736  
See  H7875

title: H7875 · siyd
text:
from 7874; lime (as boiling when slacked):--lime, plaister. 
 

See  H7874

title: H7876 · shayah
text: a primitive root; to keep in memory:--be unmindful. (Render Deuteronomy 32:18, "A Rock bore thee, thou must recollect; and (yet) thou hast forgotten," etc.)

title: H7877 · Shiyza'
text: of unknown derivation; Shiza, an Is.:--Shiza.

title: H7878 · siyach
text: a primitive root; to ponder, i.e. (by implication) converse (with oneself, and hence, aloud) or (transitively) utter:-- commune, complain, declare, meditate, muse, pray, speak, talk (with).

title: H7879 · siyach
text:
from 7878; a contemplation; by implication, an utterance:--babbling, communication, complaint, meditation, prayer, talk. 
 

See  H7878

title: H7880 · siyach
text:
from 7878; a shoot (as if uttered or put forth), i.e. (generally) shrubbery:--bush, plant, shrub. 
 

See  H7878

title: H7881 · siychah
text:
feminine of 7879; reflection; be extension, devotion:--meditation, prayer. 
 

See  H7879

title: H7882 · shiychah
text:
for 7745; a pit-fall:--pit. 
 

See  H7745

title: H7883 · Shiychowr
text:
or Shichowr {shee-khore'}; or Shichor {shee-khore'}; probably from 7835; dark, i.e. turbid; Shichor, a stream of Egypt:--Shihor, Sihor. 
 

See  H7835

title: H7884 · Shiychowr Libnath
text:
from the same as 7883 and 3835; darkish whiteness; Shichor-Libnath, a stream of Palestine:--Shihor-libnath. 
 

See  H7883  
See  H3835

title: H7885 · shayit
text:
from 7751; an oar; also (compare 7752) a scourge (figuratively):--oar, scourge. 
 

See  H7751  
See  H7752

title: H7886 · Shiyloh
text:
from 7951; tranquil; Shiloh, an epithet of the Messiah:--Shiloh. 
 

See  H7951

title: H7887 · Shiyloh
text:
or Shiloh {shee-lo'}; or Shiylow {shee-lo'}; or Shilow {shee-lo'}; from the same as 7886; Shiloh, a place in Palestine:--Shiloh. 
 

See  H7886

title: H7888 · Shiylowniy
text:
or Shiyloniy {shee-lo-nee'}; or Shiloniy {shee-lo-nee'}; from 7887; a Shilonite or inhabitant of Shiloh:--Shilonite. 
 

See  H7887

title: H7889 · Shiymown
text:
apparently for 3452; desert; Shimon, an Israelite:--Shimon. 
 

See  H3452

title: H7890 · shayin
text: from an unused root meaning to urinate; urine:--piss.

title: H7891 · shiyr
text:
or (the original form) shuwr (1 Sam. 18:6) {shoor}; a primitive root (identical with 7788 through the idea of strolling minstrelsy); to sing:--behold (by mistake for 7789), sing(-er, -ing man, - ing woman). 
 

See  H7788  
See  H7789

title: H7892 · shiyr
text:
or feminine shiyrah {shee-raw'}; from 7891; a song; abstractly, singing:--musical(-ick), X sing(-er, -ing), song. 
 

See  H7891

title: H7893 · shayish
text:
from an unused root meaning to bleach, i.e. whiten; white, i.e. marble. See 8336. 
 

See  H8336

title: H7894 · Shiysah'
text:
from the same as 7893; whiteness; Shisha, an Israelite:--Shisha. 
 

See  H7893

title: H7895 · Shiyshaq
text: or Shuwshaq {shoo-shak'}; of Egyptian derivation; Shishak, an Egyptian king:--Shishak.

title: H7896 · shiyth
text: a primitive root; to place (in a very wide application):--apply, appoint, array, bring, consider, lay (up), let alone, X look, make, mark, put (on), + regard, set, shew, be stayed, X take.

title: H7897 · shiyth
text:
from 7896; a dress (as put on):--attire. 
 

See  H7896

title: H7898 · shayith
text:
from 7896; scrub or trash, i.e. wild growth of weeds or briers (as if put on the field):--thorns. 
 

See  H7896

title: H7899 · sek
text:
from 5526 in the sense of 7753; a brier (as of a hedge):--prick. 
 

See  H5526  
See  H7753

title: H7900 · sok
text:
from 5526 in the sense of 7753; a booth (as interlaced):--tabernacle. 
 

See  H5526  
See  H7753

title: H7901 · shakab
text: a primitive root; to lie down (for rest, sexual connection, decease or any other purpose):--X at all, cast down, ((lover-))lay (self) (down), (make to) lie (down, down to sleep, still with), lodge, ravish, take rest, sleep, stay.

title: H7902 · sh@kabah
text:
from 7901; a lying down (of dew, or for the sexual act):--X  carnally, copulation, X lay, seed. 
 

See  H7901

title: H7903 · sh@kobeth
text:
from 7901; a (sexual) lying with:--X lie. 
 

See  H7901

title: H7904 · shakah
text:
a primitive root; to roam (through lust):--in the morning (by mistake for 7925). 
 

See  H7925

title: H7905 · sukkah
text:
feminine of 7900 in the sense of 7899; a dart (as pointed like a thorn):--barbed iron. 
 

See  H7900  
See  H7899

title: H7906 · Sekuw
text: from an unused root apparently meaning to surmount; an observatory (with the article); Seku, a place in Palestine:--Sechu.

title: H7907 · sekviy
text:
from the same as 7906; observant, i.e. (concretely) the mind:--heart. 
 

See  H7906

title: H7908 · sh@kowl
text:
infinitive of 7921; bereavement:--loss of children, spoiling. 
 

See  H7921

title: H7909 · shakkuwl
text:
or shakkul {shak-kool'}; from 7921; bereaved:--barren, bereaved (robbed) of children (whelps). 
 

See  H7921

title: H7910 · shikkowr
text:
or shikkor {shik-kore'}; from 7937; intoxicated, as a state or a habit:--drunk(-ard, -en, -en man). 
 

See  H7937

title: H7911 · shakach
text: or shakeach {shaw-kay'-akh}; a primitive root; to mislay, i.e. to be oblivious of, from want of memory or attention:--X  at all, (cause to) forget.

title: H7912 · sh@kach (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 7911 through the idea of disclosure of a covered or forgotten thing; to discover (literally or figuratively):--find. 
 

See  H7911

title: H7913 · shakeach
text:
from 7911; oblivious:--forget. 
 

See  H7911

title: H7914 · s@kiyah
text:
feminine from the same as 7906; a conspicuous object:--picture. 
 

See  H7906

title: H7915 · sakkiyn
text:
intensive perhaps from the same as 7906 in the sense of 7753; a knife (as pointed or edged):--knife. 
 

See  H7906  
See  H7753

title: H7916 · sakiyr
text:
from 7936; a man at wages by the day or year:--hired (man, servant), hireling. 
 

See  H7936

title: H7917 · s@kiyrah
text:
feminine of 7916; a hiring:--that is hired. 
 

See  H7916

title: H7918 · shakak
text: a primitive root; to weave (i.e. lay) a trap; figuratively, (through the idea of secreting) to allay (passions; physically, abate a flood):--appease, assuage, make to cease, pacify, set.

title: H7919 · sakal
text: a primitive root; to be (causatively, make or act) circumspect and hence, intelligent:--consider, expert, instruct, prosper, (deal) prudent(-ly), (give) skill(-ful), have good success, teach, (have, make to) understand(-ing), wisdom, (be, behave self, consider, make) wise(- ly), guide wittingly.

title: H7920 · s@kal (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) corresponding to 7919:--consider. 
 

See  H7919

title: H7921 · shakol
text: a primitive root; properly, to miscarry, i.e. suffer abortion; by analogy, to bereave (literally or figuratively):--bereave (of children), barren, cast calf (fruit, young), be (make) childless, deprive, destroy, X  expect, lose children, miscarry, rob of children, spoil.

title: H7922 · sekel
text:
or sekel {say'-kel}; from 7919; intelligence; by implication, success:--discretion, knowledge, policy, prudence, sense, understanding, wisdom, wise. 
 

See  H7919

title: H7923 · shikkuliym
text:
plural from 7921; childlessness (by continued bereavements):--to have after loss of others. 
 

See  H7921

title: H7924 · sokl@thanuw (Aramaic)
text:
(Aramaic) from 7920; intelligence:--understanding. 
 

See  H7920

title: H7925 · shakam
text:
a primitive root; properly, to incline (the shoulder to a burden); but used only as denominative from 7926; literally, to load up (on the back of man or beast), i.e. to start early in the morning:--(arise, be up, get (oneself) up, rise up) early (betimes), morning. 
 

See  H7926

title: H7926 · sh@kem
text:
from 7925; the neck (between the shoulders) as the place of burdens; figuratively, the spur of a hill:--back, X consent, portion, shoulder. 
 

See  H7925

title: H7927 · Sh@kem
text:
the same as 7926; ridge; Shekem, a place in Palestine:--Shechem. 
 

See  H7926

title: H7928 · Shekem
text:
for 7926; Shekem, the name of a Hivite and two Israelites:--Shechem. 
 

See  H7926

title: H7929 · shikmah
text:
feminine of 7926; the shoulder-bone:--shoulder blade. 
 

See  H7926

title: H7930 · Shikmiy
text:
patronymic from 7928; a Shikmite (collectively), or descendants of Shekem:--Shichemites. 
 

See  H7928
